dataset_metadata.description: The PubMed dataset is a large-scale corpus for long-form abstractive summarization. It contains scientific articles from the PubMed database, where the full-text body of the article is used as the source text and the corresponding abstract serves as the ground-truth summary. It is characterized by highly technical medical terminology and significantly longer input sequences than standard news datasets.

schema_analysis.description: The main body text of the medical research paper, typically including sections like Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.
The author-written summary of the article, providing the study's objective, methods, and key findings.
A string containing the titles of the various sections found within the article body.

structural_logic.relationships: The 'article' content is the source sequence for the 'abstract' target. 'section_names' serves as structural metadata that outlines the organization of the 'article' text.
structural_logic.label_dynamics: High compression ratio requiring domain-specific extraction; abstracts are dense with technical results and specialized entities.
structural_logic.potential_bottlenecks: Input length often exceeds standard transformer context windows (512 or 1024 tokens); presence of specialized medical jargon, abbreviations, and citation markers can affect tokenization and coherence.
